DEVCON Kids · Inspire. Enable. Empower. · code.org International Partner

Computer science and AI for every Filipino child

Founded in 2018 as a program of DEVCON Philippines, DEVCON Kids is the country’s largest tech education initiative for children: fun on the outside, serious learning inside, and run by volunteers who pay it forward.

Volunteer to learn and serveSponsor a code camp
2025 impact report

A year of hands-on learning

  • 5,609Students reached

  • 70Schools engaged

  • 10 DEVCON Kids chapters
  • 83 events in 2025
Why it matters

The demand is here. The time to act is now.

Filipino 15-year-olds ranked 77th of 81 countries in science literacy in PISA 2022, and the country placed last of 58 in math and science in TIMSS 2019. The gap is widest in rural and underserved communities.

Our vision: Filipino youth inspired by, enabled, and empowered with computer science, ready for the future.

Our mission: equitable access to foundational computer science, so children build confidence in computing, grow their interest in STEM and STEM careers, and use computing to solve problems.

Our programs

Fun on the outside, serious learning inside

K–12 standards-aligned computer science, from blocks to text: Hour of Code and Hour of AI, animation and game dev, micro:bit and mBot robotics, then HTML, CSS, Python, and C++ with Arduino and IoT.

  • Hour of Code and Hour of AI

    A first hour of computer science and AI literacy in public schools, taught by trained teachers and volunteers.

    Hour of AI case study

  • Code camps

    micro:bit Explorers, micro:bit Creative Robotics (Smart Animals, Robotics in Space), and machine learning with image classifiers.

    micro:bit case study

  • Robotics playground

    mBot races and robotics challenges where kids build, test, and compete.

  • Lead Learner workshops

    Teachers and adult volunteers learn to teach CS, in person and online, so learning continues after we leave.

    DEVCON for Educators case study
2026 so far

Strong momentum, especially in Mindanao

Over the past six months we’ve grown our chapter network and facilitator pipeline while running a steady cadence of hands-on events.

Field caravans to underserved areas

The AI Angat Mindanao Caravan brought programming and AI literacy directly to schools in Bukidnon and Iligan: 210 students and 30 teachers.

Read the caravan case study

A maturing facilitator pipeline

The CodeAI International Facilitator Training onboarded about 20 facilitators toward certification, building capacity for future rollouts.

Hackathons, end to end

PromptWars gave students a real build experience, and we demoed hardware and AI projects like KAI, our Jetson-based robot.

An operational backbone

A shared kit and inventory tracker across chapter coordinators made procurement and logistics far smoother.

From curiosity to capability

  • 86%reported more confidence in coding
  • 78%showed interest in STEM careers
  • 92%want to keep learning computer science

Hello, Code! Pangasinan brought 50 Grade 6 students into a four-hour build day, and the second Computer Science Summit trained 43 teachers from 15 Philippine Science High School campuses to teach with the BBC micro:bit.

Hour of AI 2026

Milestones: Hour of AI 2026

Our biggest school season of the year, run by every DEVCON Kids chapter with trained teachers and volunteers.

  • Execution windowsNov 23–26 and Dec 7–18, 2026. Schools pick any date inside these.
  • Free volunteer and teacher trainingNov 14, 21, and 28, open to all teachers and volunteers.
  • Awards nightHour of AI and Chapter Awards Night, Feb 5, 2027.

  1. School contacting

    • Initial outreach sentSep 11–18
    • Follow-up and interest confirmedBy Oct 9
    • Commitments and agreements collectedOct 30
    • Specific-date bookings confirmed (written or MOA)Oct 30

  2. Preparation and training

    • Readiness checkpoint: materials and venueNov 15
    • Logistics arrangedNov 15
    • Internal trainingNov 7
    • Training open to all teachers and volunteersNov 14, 21, 28
    • School readiness check with school officialsNov 15
    • Volunteer readiness check: training and reporting instructionsNov 20

  3. Execution

    • Wave 1 school visitsNov 23–27
    • Wave 1 liquidation and debriefNov 27–28
    • Wave 2 school visitsDec 7–18
    • Wave 2 liquidation and debriefDec 19

  4. Post event

    • Liquidation and report submittedDec 19
    • Impact report completedJan 18, 2027
    • Publish and thank partners weekJan 25, 2027
    • Hour of AI and Chapter Awards NightFeb 5, 2027
